title: The cone lift attached to a lifted augmentation through an extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with the complexes, ordinary derived category, shifts, localization $Q$ and cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X,N,E$ be objects of $\mathcal E$. Let $P$ be a cochain complex with $P^i=0$ for $i>0$, put $P_n=P^{-n}$ and $\partial_n=d_P^{-n}$ for $n\geq1$, and let $e:P\to X[0]$ be a quasi-isomorphism. Let $0\to N\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{p}X\to0$ be a short exact sequence of objects [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] and let $\ell:P_0\to E$ satisfy $p\ell=e^0$.

There is a unique $f:P_1\to N$ with $if=\ell\partial_1$, and $f\partial_2=0$. Let $\bar f:P\to N[1]$ have sole possibly nonzero component $f$ in degree $-1$. The cone $C(i)$ of $i:N[0]\to E[0]$ has $N$ in degree $-1$, $E$ in degree zero, and differential $i$. Its projection is $\operatorname{pr}:C(i)\to N[1]$ (so the cone triangle arrow is $-\operatorname{pr}$). The map $v:C(i)\to X[0]$ given by $p$ in degree zero is a quasi-isomorphism: $H^{-1}(C(i))=0$, $H^0(C(i))\cong X$ through $p$, and all other cohomology objects vanish. The components $\kappa^{-1}=f$, $\kappa^0=\ell$, and zero in other degrees define a cochain map $\kappa:P\to C(i)$ satisfying
$$v\kappa=e,\qquad \operatorname{pr}\kappa=\bar f.$$
Consequently $Q(\kappa)=Q(v)^{-1}Q(e)$ in $D(\mathcal E)$. These assertions hold for arbitrary such $P,e,\ell$, with no projectivity assumption on the terms of $P$.

proof.text: Because $e$ is a cochain map, $e^0\partial_1=0$. Thus $p\ell\partial_1=e^0\partial_1=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-short-exact-kernel] to the given short exact sequence with $T=P_1$ and $\varphi=\ell\partial_1$. It gives a unique $f:P_1\to N$ with $if=\ell\partial_1$. The short exactness hypotheses and monicity of $i$ are exactly those of [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

proof.text: The complex identity gives i(f∂₂)=ℓ∂₁∂₂=0. Monicity of i gives f∂₂=0. Construct the degree-one cocycle α from P to N[0] by HomComplex.Cocycle.toSingleMk, with sole component f in degree -1. After the cone lift κ is constructed, define fbar as κ followed by minus the cone triangle arrow. The triangle arrow is minus projection, so the component formula for mappingCone.lift shows that fbar has component f in degree -1; its other components vanish because N[1] is zero in those degrees. This uses the shift and cochain-map definitions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and monicity from [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone), with the shift and cochain-map definitions; elementary component calculation.

proof.text: In the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], C(i) has N in degree -1, E in degree zero, differential i, and triangle arrow minus projection. Define β as the degree-zero cochain with component ℓ. The identity if=ℓ∂₁ gives δβ+αi=0 by HomComplex.Cochain.δ_toSingleMk and toSingleMk_postcomp. Apply mappingCone.lift to α and β to obtain κ. Its first and second projections in degrees -1 and zero are f and ℓ, respectively. In all other degrees the cone terms are zero, so κ has zero components. The map v is mappingCone.descShortComplex of the single-degree image of the given sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Its degree-zero component is the second projection followed by p, by the two summand identities for descShortComplex.

proof.text: The category of cochain complexes is abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact]. The single-degree functor preserves finite limits and colimits, so ShortComplex.ShortExact.map_of_exact maps the given sequence to a short exact sequence of complexes. This directly supplies the short exactness needed in [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso], applied via mappingCone.quasiIso_descShortComplex. Thus v is a quasi-isomorphism. For r≠0, transport the zero homology of X[0] across the isomorphism H^r(v). In degree zero, compose the isomorphism H^0(v) with singleObjHomologySelfIso. These are the homology and quasi-isomorphism constructions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), preceding construction of the cone quasi-isomorphism; degreewise exactness is Tag 0114 (homology-lemma-cat-cochain-abelian).

proof.text: The sole possibly nonzero component of $v\kappa$ is $p\ell=e^0$ in degree zero, so $v\kappa=e$. The sole possibly nonzero component of $\operatorname{pr}\kappa$ is $f$ in degree $-1$, so $\operatorname{pr}\kappa=\bar f$. Apply the localization functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $Q(v)Q(\kappa)=Q(e)$, and $Q(v)$ is invertible because $v$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Left multiplication by its inverse gives $Q(\kappa)=Q(v)^{-1}Q(e)$. These arguments used only the supplied lift $\ell$, the short exact sequence, and cochain equations, so apply to every stated $P,e,\ell$ without projective terms.
